paper.title: Algorithm 883: SparsePOP---A Sparse Semidefinite Programming Relaxation of Polynomial Optimization Problems
paper.venue: ACM TOMS 35(2), Article 15 (Jul 2008); paper text not reachable in this wake (not searched; the archive's Doc/ manual is the source used)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 883.zip (scouted 2026-11-27, sha256 2c05deedb393a2959240791cf94d27ebd8e3617eb7bed620415d31b8b2b4123e). MATLAB/Octave tree 883/SparsePOP200/ (sparsePOP.m, example1.m, example1.gms, subPrograms/) plus its manual 883/Doc/UserManual/sect3.tex. The solver SeDuMi is NOT in the archive; the rerun must obtain it (GPL, free) and an Octave or MATLAB interpreter.

claim.location: Shipped user manual Doc/UserManual/sect3.tex (section 'The GAMS scalar format'): the printed output of sparsePOP('example1.gms', param) with param.relaxOrder = 3 and SeDuMi eps 1e-9 (SparsePOP 2.00). The example is the POP of example1.m (minimize -2x1+3x2-2x3 subject to a quadratic inequality, two linear inequalities, one linear equality and box bounds). The claim is the line POP.objValue, the approximated optimal value of that POP.
claim.metric: POP.objValue printed by printSolution.m for example1.gms, relaxOrder 3, SeDuMi eps 1e-9
claim.paper_value: -7.9550951 (manual printout; the paper text was not checked, so no printed table value was located)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference is printed to 8 significant digits, a rounding step of 5e-8; the same manual reports relative objective error 1.086e-9 from SeDuMi at eps 1e-9. 1e-6 absolute covers print rounding and solver-version noise about 20 times over, yet is far below the difference between the relaxOrder=3 value and a different relaxation (SDPobjValue -7.9550950 is itself a bound of the same order). Not loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute for the example (manual reports 0.05 s conversion and 0.27 s SeDuMi); plus interpreter and SeDuMi install.
cost.data_size: None beyond the archive (about 3 MB zip; the GMS and SDPA sample files are not needed).
cost.data_licence: GPL (SparsePOP and SeDuMi are GPL per the archive's Doc/GPL.txt); the rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The shipped manual prints a numerical SDP-relaxation optimum for a small POP, which the SparsePOP code must compute from the sparse moment relaxation, so the number cannot be obtained by reading the code.
